findings.claim: The machine-specific path verifier still misses Windows drive-root Flint paths written with forward slashes.
findings.evidence: The acceptance evidence requires cross-platform absolute Flint-root rejection, but `findMachineSpecificPath` only matches Windows drive roots with backslashes via `/[A-Za-z]:\\(?:[^\\\s"'`]+\\)*?(?:flint-realtime-fabric|flint-gate|flint-forge)(?:\\|$)/i`; the added regression in `tests/release/v3-flint-portable-contracts.test.mjs` covers `D:\\checkouts\\flint-gate...` but not common config forms such as `D:/checkouts/flint-gate/src/index.ts`.
findings.suggested_fix: Match both separators for Windows drive-root Flint paths, e.g. use `[\\/]` throughout the drive-root pattern, and add a `D:/checkouts/flint-gate/...` regression.

findings.claim: The JWT value scanner can miss valid JWT-shaped service-role tokens whose signature segment ends with a base64url non-word character.
findings.evidence: `containsServiceRoleJwt` extracts candidates with `/\beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]*\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\b/g`; because the trailing `\b` only succeeds after a word character, a JWT whose final signature character is `-` is not matched even though `-` is allowed by the `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` base64url character set and the acceptance criterion requires rejecting service-role JWT values.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the trailing word-boundary with explicit delimiter lookarounds such as `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_-])([A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]*)(?![A-Za-z0-9_-])`, then decode candidates and add a regression with a service-role JWT ending in `-`.
